This is a rebalance storm.
Each rebalance creates more lag and more replayed work, which makes the next batch slower, which gets the next worker evicted.

Why the fix works.
With 50 records per poll, a batch finishes in seconds, far inside the 5-minute deadline, so nobody is mistaken for dead.
The index removes the real slowness.
Consumption now runs above production, so the lag drains.

Recovered.

A slower dependency quietly pushed batch time past a timeout, and the group's own recovery mechanism amplified it.
The report has the takeaways.
Each worker polls 500 records, then must poll again within max poll interval equals 300000.
Heartbeats run on a separate thread, so a slow loop is the only way to look dead.
Range assignor + eager protocol: all 6 partitions are revoked from all 3 workers, the group re-joins and syncs, about 22 seconds here, before anyone consumes again.
The replayed records hit the same unindexed query.
Pool use climbs toward its 40-connection limit, so queries also queue for a connection.
Commits after each eviction fail with CommitFailedException: the work was done, then handed to another member and done again.
The index turns a 180 thousand-row scan into an index lookup; 50 records times about 60 milliseconds about 3 seconds per batch, two orders of magnitude under the 300 seconds limit.
Worth adding: partition assignment strategy equals CooperativeStickyAssignor and group instance id, static membership, so one slow worker cannot stop the others.

A payments team consumes an orders topic with three workers. A database migration makes each record slower to process. Nobody's consumer crashes, yet within minutes the group is stuck in a loop of rebalances and lag is climbing.
The system.

checkout-api publishes every order to a 6-partition orders topic. Three payments workers form one consumer group and charge the orders, each polling a batch of up to 500 records, processing them one by one against Postgres, then committing.
How it normally works.

A worker must call poll again within max poll interval, 5 minutes. If it does not, the group coordinator decides it is dead, removes it, and rebalances: partitions are reassigned to whoever is left. Normally a batch takes seconds and this never comes up.
Today.
A database migration adds a fraud score lookup with no index yet, which makes each record about 650 milliseconds slower. Nothing crashes and nothing alerts.
Here is the system: checkout-api, orders topic, payments-worker-1, payments-worker-2, payments-worker-3 and payments-db.
What happened.
A slow query made batches outlast the 5-minute poll deadline. Kafka evicted healthy workers, and each eager rebalance made the next eviction more likely: a storm.
The numbers.
Consumer lag: 79.2 thousand msgs at worst, and 400 msgs at the end.
DB 99th percentile: 1.1 seconds at worst, and 60 milliseconds at the end.
Rebalances: 3 at worst, and 0 at the end.
Takeaway 1.
Size batches to the timeout.
Worst-case batch time must stay well under max poll interval.
Takeaway 2.
Prefer cooperative rebalancing.
Cooperative-sticky and static membership keep unaffected workers consuming.
Takeaway 3.
Make replays cheap.
Idempotent processing and frequent commits make redone work harmless.
Takeaway 4.
Don't scale out mid-storm.
New consumers trigger another rebalance; fix the slow dependency first.
How it happened.
Migration 0042: query about 650 milliseconds slower.
500-record batch > max poll interval.
Healthy worker evicted as dead.
Eager rebalance stops every worker.
Replay + lag load the slow DB.
Fix: 50-record batches + index.

Some common myths.
Myth: Add more workers.
Every new worker triggers another rebalance, and more workers means more partitions reassigned while the group is already unstable.
Myth: The workers are crashing.
They were healthy. Kafka removed them for being slow to call poll, which looks identical to dead from the coordinator's side.
